metadata.note: The Susquehanna and New York Railroad (S&NY), Towanda - Monroeton - Laquin - Masten - Marsh Hill Junction, Pennsylvania, with its 1904 Ralston terminus and Gray's Run Branch, plus its predecessor the Barclay Railroad (Towanda - Barclay). A lumber-boom mountain road formed in 1902 from the Binghamton, Towanda & Western, which had rebuilt the flood-wrecked Barclay Railroad; abandoned 1942 (ICC; last scheduled run 23 May 1942). Drawn only for the years the research report confirms (S&NY 1903/1904 - 1934, both ends open; Ralston and Gray's Run Branch 1904 anchors; Barclay Railroad 1875 - 1884, both ends open). Research report: research/branches/susquehanna_and_new_york_railroad.txt.

omitted: Marsh Hill Junction - West Williamsport over the PRR (report block [6]): drawable NONE - no S&NY passenger train south of Ralston/Marsh Hill is confirmed by any timetable, despite Wikipedia's 'between Williamsport and Towanda'. The PRR track is already drawn as Northern Central: Baltimore - Elmira.
Gray's Run Branch beyond Grays Run (Yoder Run, Wilkinson, McCracken Summit, Frozen Run): log railroad, no passenger evidence.
Binghamton, Towanda and Western (c.1900-1902, report block [8]): no evidence it ran a passenger train under its own name.
Susquehanna and Eagles Mere Railroad (Masten - Hillsgrove, 3 ft, report block [9]): a separate company; no confirmable passenger year.
State Line and Sullivan / LV Bernice Branch (Towanda - Monroeton - Bernice, report block [10]): a Lehigh Valley-system road, not an S&NY predecessor; left to Lehigh Valley research.

Original Wheelerville - Ellenton (1st) - Masten alignment (report block [4]): not a separate feature (relocation date unknown); traced and described in the East Laquin - Marsh Hill Junction feature's geometry_quality.

Freight-only afterlife: Towanda - Monroeton bought by the LV in 1942 and kept for freight; the Ralston coal spur of the late 1930s; the Barclay incline and mine trackage; logging lines feeding the S&NY; 1942 salvage trains (Rule 1).
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END, all S&NY main-line features (Towanda - East Laquin, East Laquin - Marsh Hill Junction): passenger service is confirmed only to the 14 Oct 1934 employee timetable No. 47 (known through snyrr.com). Late-1930s mixed-train photos (one datable to 1937 or later by a boxcar type) suggest later service; the last scheduled run was 23 May 1942 but is not stated to have carried passengers. Best next sources: Kaseman pp.10-24; the 1942 ICC abandonment decision; any 1935-1942 Official Guide entry for the S&NY.

OPEN START: S&NY passenger service is confirmed from 1903 (East Laquin in the 1903 Guide station list) north of Laquin and from 1904 (company timetable) south of it; 1902 (company formed, Laquin founded) and a 1903 through route are possible but unproven.
Barclay Railroad: both ends open (Guide anchors 1875 and 1884 only); its operator after the Towanda Coal Co. lease (c.1876?) and whether it ran via Monroeton on its own line are unknown.

Ralston terminus: 1904 anchor only; when S&NY passenger trains stopped running to Ralston and began terminating at Marsh Hill is unknown. Mileage conflict Marsh Hill Junction - Ralston: 0.8 mi (BL S&NY section) vs 2.9 mi (BL PRR section; Wikipedia's '3 mi north of Bodines'); the OSM grade supports the longer.
Gray's Run Branch: 1904 anchor only; passenger end unknown (mill closed c.1910).

Date of the Wheelerville - Ellenton - Masten relocation (probably the 1906 rebuild; before the 1918-19 valuation map). The identification of OSM way 866883967 as the original alignment is an inference from snyrr.com's valuation-map discussion.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh on every feature are estimates (see each speed_source and segment note); no Official Guide page for the S&NY was read directly.

Ways: Towanda Industrial Track 1212911467/68/75/76, 96810299, 926407693 (still partly in use as a Lehigh Valley/successor industrial track, but tagged with this road as old operator); abandoned grade 672786424/25, 10726095, 10686101, 683621084/85/87/88, 170994257, 672786419/20, 809168995/96, 170994202, 170994256. 0.12 mi of an untagged active siding (1112817153) at the Towanda end.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 14.98 mi against 15.3 mi documented (BL s.455 mileposts, Towanda 0.0 - East Laquin 15.3; -2%). Per-station check against BL: Monroeton traced 3.8 (BL 3.8), Weston 7.0 (BL 7.6), Long Valley 11.3 (BL 11.8), Barclay/foot of plane 14.0 (BL 14.3). Everything is on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Susquehanna and New York Railroad EXCEPT one gap: STRAIGHT LINES Monroeton - Powell (1.7 mi) and Powell - Weston (1.5 mi), 3.2 mi against 3.8 mi documented (BL 3.8 - 7.6), where no grade is mapped. The bend point is hand-pinned at the Towanda Creek / Schrader Creek confluence at the hamlet of Powell (BL 4.8 'Powell [Hawes]'), since the line went west up Towanda Creek to Powell and then south up Schrader Creek to Weston; the chords cut the valley curves, which is most of the 0.6 mi shortfall there (Greenwood, BL 5.7, lies on the Powell - Weston chord). East Laquin is placed by milepost (1.6 mi short of Laquin by BL), not at a mapped station site. The Towanda end starts where the tagged S&NY track ends near the Lehigh Valley at the south side of Towanda (41.760 N), about 0.8 km south of the town centre; BL puts the S&NY's own Towanda station 0.3 mi before Washington Street, so the first few hundred metres to the LV station are not drawn. Between Weston and Barclay the line was rebuilt in 1902-03 over the 1850s Barclay Railroad; BL marks Lamoka (10.9) 'reloc?', so small local relocations of that rebuild are drawn as OSM has them.

segments.note: Susquehanna and New York Railroad (formed 1902 from the Binghamton, Towanda & Western, which had bought and rebuilt the flood-wrecked Barclay Railroad). START 1903 is the earliest CONFIRMED year: East Laquin (then 'Sugar Run') appears in the 1903 Official Guide station list (BL s.455); passenger service in 1902 is possible but unproven. The 1904 company timetable shows three round trips Towanda - Ralston (Abell p.68 via WP); 78,000 passengers carried in 1906 (Abell p.68). END YEAR IS [OPEN]: 1934 is the last CONFIRMED year (S&NY employee timetable No. 47, in effect 14 Oct 1934, carding first-class trains 5/6 between Marsh Hill and Towanda, known through snyrr.com), not a known end. Late-1930s photos show trains 5/6 running as mixed trains with a combine carrying the markers (engine #119, bought 1934; one photo datable to 1937 or later by a boxcar type), and the S&NY's last scheduled run was 23 May 1942 (Kaseman p.24 / Abell p.43 via Wikipedia), but no source seen says passengers rode after 1934 or that the 1942 run carried any. Do not extend without evidence. Under USRA federal control 1918-1920 the road was 'placed under control of the Lehigh Valley' (Kaseman p.10 via WP) with its own crews and equipment; not treated as a change of operator. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE spanning the era: the 1904 timetable shows three round trips Towanda - Ralston (Abell p.68 via WP), Kaseman p.9 says two round trips a day 'during the early years of the 20th century', and the 1934 employee timetable shows one first-class train each way. Not a timetable reading for any single year. After 1942 the LV bought Towanda - Monroeton and kept it for freight - not drawn (Rule 1).

No Official Guide page for the road was read directly. Headway is an estimate.

All on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Susquehanna and New York Railroad (plus 0.18 mi untagged abandoned grade at Marsh Hill); no straight-line legs. Per-station check (cumulative from Towanda): Laquin 16.6 (BL 16.9), Wheelerville 26.0 (BL 27.1), Ellenton 29.0 (BL 29.5), Masten 33.7 (BL 32.5), Crandalltown 38.1 (BL 36.3), Marsh Hill Junction 43.0 (BL 42.0). opstrace's despike step was turned OFF for this line because it cut a genuine 2-mi horseshoe below Ellenton (the loop east to 76.798 W and back towards Masten) - see research/notes/opstrace-despike-cuts-real-hairpins.md. LATER ALIGNMENT THAN PART OF ITS ERA (Rule 2): between Wheelerville and Masten this draws the RE-ALIGNED main line via Ellenton (2nd) and the horseshoe, 12.1 mi Wheelerville - Crandalltown. The ORIGINAL 1904 route via Ellenton (1st) (BL s.455 note '** 1. Former route until?') also survives in OSM - way 866883967 (name='Susquehanna & New York', no operator tag) running direct SW from just north of Ellenton, then untagged abandoned ways and 'Old Loggers Path' (987613790, 890693647, 890693644-46, 926046417/18, 890693642) through Masten to Masten Road 492827780 - 9.9 mi Wheelerville - Crandalltown, which matches BL's mileposts (9.2 mi) better, so BL's station list probably dates from the original route. Identifying 866883967 as the original line rests on snyrr.com's reading of the 1918-19 valuation map ('the long spur north of Ellenton ... is the remnants of the Central Pennsylvania Logging Co. logging railroad and the original S&NY alignment to Masten'); that is an inference, not a dated source. The relocation date is unknown (probably the 1906 grade-easing rebuild, Kaseman p.8; certainly before the 1918-19 valuation map), so the original route is not drawn as a separate feature and the 1904 to c.1906 years are shown on the later alignment. Marsh Hill Junction is drawn at the end of the S&NY grade beside the PRR Elmira Branch near Marsh Hill (41.471 N); the S&NY's own spur north to Ralston is a separate 1904 feature.

properties.speed_source: estimated from two timetables only: 1904, about 2 h for the ~43 mi Towanda - Ralston (Abell p.68 via WP, ~35 km/h); 1934, train 5 Marsh Hill 9:10 - Towanda 11:06 (snyrr.com, ~36 km/h). Mountain line with helper grades over the Ellenton summit; intermediate stops not timed.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 2.87 mi on the S&NY's own tagged track (way 170994290), no straight legs. MILEAGE CONFLICT, unresolved: BL's S&NY section gives Marsh Hill Junction 42.0 - Ralston 42.8 (0.8 mi), BL's PRR section puts the two 2.9 mi apart (PRR mp 113.9 / 116.8), and Wikipedia puts Marsh Hill Junction 3 mi north of Bodines. The OSM grade supports the longer figure: the S&NY ran up the east side of Lycoming Creek from the Marsh Hill end of its line to Ralston on its own rails, not over the PRR. The way continues north of Ralston to about 41.52 N (the late-1930s coal spur 'up the branch to Ralston' was freight); only the part to Ralston is drawn.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1904 is the single proven year: the 1904 company timetable runs S&NY passenger trains Towanda - Ralston (Abell p.68 via WP), and Ralston was 'where this line operated passenger services ... to connect with PRR trains' (WP Ralston). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed; by 1934 trains 5/6 terminated at Marsh Hill, not Ralston (snyrr.com), and when the passenger terminus moved is unknown. Do not widen without evidence. headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE from the 1904 timetable's three round trips.

properties.speed_source: estimated, unsourced: no running times for the branch were found; a lightly built lumber line.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 12.19 mi against 12.9 mi documented (BL s.456, Ralston 42.8 - Grays Run 55.7; -6%). Per-station check from Ralston: Bodines 4.9 (BL 5.1), Williamson/mouth of Gray's Run 7.9 (BL 8.1), Grays Run 12.2 (BL 12.9). APPROXIMATED legs: (1) STRAIGHT LINE 0.39 mi at the trestle over Lycoming Creek and the PRR south of Ralston, from the S&NY line to the west-bank grade; (2) STRAIGHT LINE 1.62 mi Marsh Hill - Bodines, where the branch ran beside the PRR on the west bank and no grade is mapped (the PRR Elmira Branch lies about 300 m east); (3) STREAM STAND-IN 3.29 mi from the top of the mapped grade on South Grays Run Road (41.444 N) to Grays Run (41.484 N), drawn along the Gray's Run stream centreline, which the logging grade followed but whose meanders it did not - treat this stretch as approximate to within the valley floor. The first 1.3 mi from Ralston share the S&NY Marsh Hill - Ralston geometry. Only Ralston - Grays Run is drawn: the line continued as a log railroad to Yoder Run, Wilkinson, McCracken Summit and Frozen Run (fragments in OSM as 'Grays Run RR', e.g. 1528933829/30), with no passenger evidence (BL: 'did passenger train, excursions? continue to?').

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1904 is the single proven year: BL heads the Gray's Run Branch '1904t' (the 1904 company public timetable) and Williamson appears as 'Grays' in the 1904 Official Guide station list. The S&NY bought the Gray's Run Railroad (the Central Pennsylvania Lumber Co.'s log line) in 1903; the branch was 'abandoned later when the timber industry ran its course' (WP) and the Grays Run mill closed around 1910 (WP Ralston). Service certainly ran wider than 1904 both ways, but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE (no timetable detail seen).

The first 13.8 mi are the S&NY's own tagged grade (see the Towanda - East Laquin feature); the last 0.38 mi are OSM ways 809168994, 809168993 and 704839225 (name='Barclay Railroad', railway=abandoned/razed) to the foot of the Barclay incline (locality node 'Barclay Station').
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 14.17 mi against 14.3 mi documented (BL s.455, Towanda 0.0 - Barclay [Foot of Plane] 14.3; the Bradford Reporter's '16 and 3/4 miles' of 1856 probably includes mine trackage). LATER ALIGNMENT THAN ITS ERA (Rule 2): 13.8 of the 14.2 mi are drawn on the Susquehanna and New York's 1902-03 rebuild of this road, i.e. the same geometry as the S&NY Towanda - East Laquin feature, because no separate Barclay Railroad grade is mapped there; the S&NY 'rebuilt over the ex-Barclay Railroad as far as Barclay' (report), but local relocations in that rebuild (BL marks Lamoka 'reloc?') mean the 1875-1884 line may have differed by some metres to hundreds of metres in places. Only the last 0.38 mi into the foot of the plane is on ways named for the Barclay Railroad itself. Includes the S&NY's STRAIGHT LINES Monroeton - Powell (1.7 mi) and Powell - Weston (1.5 mi). UNRESOLVED: whether the Barclay Railroad ran through Monroeton on its own line or used the parallel State Line & Sullivan between Towanda and Monroeton is not established; both are drawn here as the S&NY line. The Towanda end is the S&NY's, not the Barclay Railroad's own Towanda station, whose site was not located. The gravity incline up to Barclay village (OSM 675738983) carried coal and is not drawn.

segments.note: Barclay Railroad and Coal Company (chartered 1854; coal traffic from July 1856), leased and operated by the Towanda Coal Co. for about 20 years from c.1856 (Kaseman p.5 via WP; BL '(operated by Towanda Coal Co.)'); who ran it after the lease is not established, so the feature carries the road's own name. Steam from the start (locomotives 'Towanda' and 'Philadelphia', 1857) - no animal-power years. START 1875 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start: Barclay is the terminus of a passenger service in the 1875 Official Guide (BL letter y). END 1884 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: the station appears as 'Foot of Plane' in the 1884 Guide (BL letter q). Both ends are [OPEN] - passengers may have ridden before 1875 and after 1884 (the road was reported abandoned 1899 and wrecked by the 1900 flood), but nothing else is confirmed; continuity between the two Guide listings is assumed, not proven. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day assumed; no timetable detail seen).
